subject: Urgent: Pinecrest latency and hallucination surge after model_v6-quant rollout
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@pinecrest.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden latency & hallucination surge after this morning's update

Rachel —

We started seeing a big jump in p95 latency and an uptick in hallucinated outputs starting around 07:45 PT after you rolled model_v6-quant into our production pool. Error rate (5xx) climbed from ~0.2% to ~2.8% and median latency increased by ~120ms. In addition, our QA team is seeing higher rates of hallucination on medical entity extraction (examples attached). This is customer-impacting — a number of clinicians reported blank results or incorrect diagnoses.

I've attached a small snapshot and a few example prompts (pinecrest-error-snapshot-20260601.json) and a chart of p95 for the last 24h (slo-pinecrest-p95-20260601.png). We are pausing customer-facing launches until this is resolved. Please advise next steps and timeline.

Emily Zhao
Head of Product
Pinecrest Health

Attachments: pinecrest-error-snapshot-20260601.json (json), slo-pinecrest-p95-20260601.png (image)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@pinecrest.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency & hallucination surge after this morning's update

Emily — thanks for the quick heads-up and the artifacts. I'm escalating immediately.

Short summary of immediate actions from our side:
- I've looped in Irene (serving runtime) and Sean (ops) for a hot investigation.
- Can you confirm whether you were routed to the new v6-quant variant only, or mixed traffic? Any headers or route ids would help.
- We're preparing a canary rollback option should we need it; that would restore pre-v6 traffic within 10 minutes of approval.

Irene / Sean / Aditya: taking this to the top. Please confirm suspected root causes and a proposed mitigation timeline in the next 60 minutes. I will keep Pinecrest updated every 30 minutes.

—Rachel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@pinecrest.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency & hallucination surge after this morning's update

Team — initial triage:
- Observed: deployment of model_v6-quant rolled at 07:30 PT into the pool for Pinecrest. Traffic split was 100% after rollout; no gradual canary was applied due to a config oversight on the canary flag.
- Metrics: p95 increased from ~300ms to ~420ms; 5xx spike corresponds with token decoding stalls and repeated timeouts from the new quantized kernels.
- Quality: We see an increase in answer omission/hallucination for long-context prompts; post-quantization numerical instability in logits appears correlated.

Immediate proposal:
1) Roll back Pinecrest to model_v6-nonquant (previous stable) as an emergency mitigation. This will be a quick config flip and should restore latency and error rates to baseline within ~10–12 minutes.
2) Preserve logs and core dumps from affected nodes for postmortem.
3) Run a targeted offline verification harness on v6-quant with Pinecrest prompt set to reproduce the decoding stalls.

I'll stand by for approval to execute rollback. If we proceed, ops (Sean) will coordinate a controlled flip and we will notify Pinecrest with expected restoration ETA.

Irene Choi
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@pinecrest.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency & hallucination surge after this morning's update

Approved. Rolling back Pinecrest traffic to model_v6-nonquant now.

Plan:
- T+0m: flip routing policy to point Pinecrest pool at model_v6-nonquant. New requests will land on old variant.
- T+3m: monitor p95, 5xx, and decode stall counters.
- T+10m: full roll complete; if metrics look stable for 30 minutes, we close the incident.

Note: We're collecting kernel traces and will attach a diagnostic bundle. I'll post updates at +5, +15, +30.

Attachments: pinecrest-diagnostic-bundle-20260601.tar.gz (attached to ops ticket)

—Sean
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Emily replied (in-thread):

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@pinecrest.ai>, contracts@pinecrest.ai
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Pinecrest executive brief: root cause, mitigation, next steps

Team / Pinecrest execs — consolidated postmortem & exec summary. Sorry for the delay; we needed the full diagnostic set.

Summary (incident window: 2026-06-01 07:30 PT → 2026-06-01 10:10 PT):
- Root cause: an unintended 100% rollout of model_v6-quant to Pinecrest combined with a quantization kernel change that produced non-deterministic decoding stalls on long-context prompts. The stalls caused tokenization timeouts that cascaded into 5xx errors and perceived hallucination as partial outputs were returned.
- Impact: p95 +120ms; 5xx increased to 2.8% during the window; sample quality regressions on entity extraction for ~4% of sensitive prompts.
- Mitigation: immediate rollback to v6-nonquant at T+10m; metrics returned to baseline within 20 minutes. No customer data loss.
- Action items (owners & ETA):
  1) Serving: add a hard guard to prevent 100% variant flips without explicit canary flag (Irene) — ETA 2026-06-10
  2) Runtime: patch quant kernel for numerical stability and add decode-stall detection (Irene + Runtime) — ETA 2026-06-17
  3) QA: add Pinecrest prompt set to pre-deploy canary harness and a long-context stress test (Aditya + QA) — ETA 2026-06-12
  4) Customer: Redwood to provide Pinecrest a remediation report and a one-time service credit (Marissa + Revenue Ops) — draft contract amendment attached (pinecrest-contract-amendment-draft.pdf).

We recommend a controlled re-roll of v6-quant to a small canary (5%) behind detect-and-fallback and with Pinecrest's explicit approval.

Emily / Pinecrest: we recognize this was customer-impacting and are prepared to work with your procurement/legal on credit language. Marissa will follow up with a draft amendment and proposed credit band.

—Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pinecrest-contract-amendment-draft.pdf (PDF)
